answer: A Trie node contains a map of child character nodes (`children: Map<string, TrieNode>`) and a boolean `isEndOfWord`. Inserting a word runs in O(L) time where L is word length. On `get(key)` or `put(key, val)`, the accessed node is moved to the head. When capacity is exceeded during `put()`, the node at the tail (least recently used) is evicted from both list and map.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals (Variant #161).
answer: Sort the intervals by their start times. Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Implement a topological sort algorithm to resolve module dependency graphs and detect cyclic imports (Variant #241).
answer: Use Kahn’s algorithm (in-degree array) or DFS with 3-color node state marking (White=unvisited, Gray=in current DFS path, Black=processed). If a DFS traversal visits a Gray node, a cyclic dependency exists (e.g. A -> B -> A). The reverse post-order DFS yields the correct dependency resolution order.

If a DFS traversal visits a Gray node, a cyclic dependency exists (e.g. A -> B -> A). The reverse post-order DFS yields the correct dependency resolution order.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Implement an in-memory Prefix Trie data structure supporting insert, search, and startsWith queries (Variant #321).
answer: A Trie node contains a map of child character nodes (`children: Map<string, TrieNode>`) and a boolean `isEndOfWord`. Inserting a word runs in O(L) time where L is word length. Querying `startsWith(prefix)` traverses the trie to the prefix node and collects all descendant terminal words via DFS.

Querying `startsWith(prefix)` traverses the trie to the prefix node and collects all descendant terminal words via DFS.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) Cache with O(1) get and O(1) put time complexity (Variant #401).
answer: An LRU Cache combines a Hash Map for O(1) key-to-node lookups and a Doubly Linked List to maintain access recency order. On `get(key)` or `put(key, val)`, the accessed node is moved to the head. When capacity is exceeded during `put()`, the node at the tail (least recently used) is evicted from both list and map.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals (Variant #481).
answer: Sort the intervals by their start times. Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Implement a topological sort algorithm to resolve module dependency graphs and detect cyclic imports (Variant #561).
answer: Use Kahn’s algorithm (in-degree array) or DFS with 3-color node state marking (White=unvisited, Gray=in current DFS path, Black=processed). If a DFS traversal visits a Gray node, a cyclic dependency exists (e.g. A -> B -> A). The reverse post-order DFS yields the correct dependency resolution order.

If a DFS traversal visits a Gray node, a cyclic dependency exists (e.g. A -> B -> A). The reverse post-order DFS yields the correct dependency resolution order.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Implement an in-memory Prefix Trie data structure supporting insert, search, and startsWith queries (Variant #641).
answer: A Trie node contains a map of child character nodes (`children: Map<string, TrieNode>`) and a boolean `isEndOfWord`. Inserting a word runs in O(L) time where L is word length. Querying `startsWith(prefix)` traverses the trie to the prefix node and collects all descendant terminal words via DFS.

Querying `startsWith(prefix)` traverses the trie to the prefix node and collects all descendant terminal words via DFS.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) Cache with O(1) get and O(1) put time complexity (Variant #721).
answer: An LRU Cache combines a Hash Map for O(1) key-to-node lookups and a Doubly Linked List to maintain access recency order. On `get(key)` or `put(key, val)`, the accessed node is moved to the head. When capacity is exceeded during `put()`, the node at the tail (least recently used) is evicted from both list and map.

On `get(key)` or `put(key, val)`, the accessed node is moved to the head. When capacity is exceeded during `put()`, the node at the tail (least recently used) is evicted from both list and map.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals (Variant #801).
answer: Sort the intervals by their start times. Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

If a DFS traversal visits a Gray node, a cyclic dependency exists (e.g. A -> B -> A). The reverse post-order DFS yields the correct dependency resolution order.

On `get(key)` or `put(key, val)`, the accessed node is moved to the head. When capacity is exceeded during `put()`, the node at the tail (least recently used) is evicted from both list and map.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals (Variant #1121).
answer: Sort the intervals by their start times. Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

answer: Sort the intervals by their start times. Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

If a DFS traversal visits a Gray node, a cyclic dependency exists (e.g. A -> B -> A). The reverse post-order DFS yields the correct dependency resolution order.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals (Variant #1441).
answer: Sort the intervals by their start times. Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Implement a topological sort algorithm to resolve module dependency graphs and detect cyclic imports (Variant #1521).
answer: Use Kahn’s algorithm (in-degree array) or DFS with 3-color node state marking (White=unvisited, Gray=in current DFS path, Black=processed). If a DFS traversal visits a Gray node, a cyclic dependency exists (e.g. A -> B -> A). The reverse post-order DFS yields the correct dependency resolution order.

On `get(key)` or `put(key, val)`, the accessed node is moved to the head. When capacity is exceeded during `put()`, the node at the tail (least recently used) is evicted from both list and map.

question: [Google · L3 (Junior)] Given an array of meeting time intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals (Variant #1761).
answer: Sort the intervals by their start times. Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.

Iterate through the sorted list: if the current interval starts before or at the end time of the previous merged interval (`curr.start <= prev.end`), merge them by setting `prev.end = Math.max(prev.end, curr.end)`. Otherwise, push the current interval as a new entry. Runs in O(N log N) time.
